messages:
maria (Product): quick design review request — putting the new latency card in front of the pipeline dashboard. sketch attached (img link). goal: make p95 and throughput readable at a glance, and keep sampling controls discoverable but not dominant

jake (Design): looked — nice. question: do we want p95 as a single line or a shaded band? single line reads cleaner at small widths but band helps show variance.

sam (Eng-Frontend): single-line lighter stroke + discrete dot for p99 is easiest perf-wise. shaded band needs area rendering and can be noisy on small charts. can do band as optional toggle.

anya (A11y): whichever we choose, we need an aria description that explains "what" the chart shows and the current time range/sampling level. keyboard focus must expose exact values at hovered points. also color contrast for the band fill must meet 4.5:1 against bg.

li (Eng-ML): from infra side, sampling metadata is real-time-ish. we can return a header with "sample_rate": "auto|1%|10%|100%" and a note whether the sample is prefix or uniform. UI should show the effective TPS that sample corresponds to.

katie (PM): use cases: 1) SRE quickly checking regressions (needs p95 + p99); 2) Product dev triaging (wants quick compare across models); 3) Exec dashboard (needs compact snapshot). layout should support compact mode.

jake (Design): new proposal: compact card shows only p50/p95 sparkline + throughput spark bar; expanded modal has heatmap + time-slicer + sampling controls. compact shows a tiny badge "sampled: auto" if sample_rate != 100%.

sam (Eng-Frontend): that badge is fine. trade: avoid too many network calls when expanding. can lazy-load the heavy heatmap component on open. also recommend reusing existing timepicker component for consistency.

anya (A11y): mini-badge needs an accessible label: e.g., "Sampling: automatic (approx. 10% of requests visible)." and it should be reachable by keyboard nav. when expanded, the heatmap must have table-mode fallback for screen-readers.

maria (Product): copy ask: what should the badge say when auto? "sampled: auto (est. 10%)" or "sampled: adaptive"? pref is human-readable and actionable.

li (Eng-ML): we can compute an estimate; backend returns "sample_estimate": "~10%". but be conservative: show a range like "~8–12%" when variance is high.

jake (Design): copy suggestion: "Sampled — adaptive (~10%)" with hover tooltip: "Redwood adapts sampling to meet latency SLOs; click to adjust." keeps it short.

sam (Eng-Frontend): small nit: don't use parentheses in badge on very small screens — use tooltip instead. badge text should be max 12 chars.

anya (A11y): tooltip must be accessible. Use aria-describedby pointing to an offscreen tooltip element when focused.

maria (Product): UX flow question: where should sampling controls live? inline in expanded card, or a global per-dashboard setting?

katie (PM): recommend 2 layers: per-dashboard global default + per-card override. that matches how teams often want to tune cost vs fidelity.

li (Eng-ML): agreeing with 2 layers; API will accept card_override in request header. example header: `X-Redwood-Sample: 10%`

sam (Eng-Frontend): implementation plan: compact card + expand modal. modal contains: large p95 chart, throughput histogram, heatmap (lazy), time-slicer, and sampling dropdown with options [auto, 100%, 10%, 1%, custom]. keyboard & touch friendly.

jake (Design): visual: propose darker axis lines, thinner grid, highlight selected time range with subtle rounded rect; spacing tokens: `--space-2` between spark and badge. attaching figma frames.

maria (Product): accessibility + copy ownership? anya can you draft the a11y copy, and jake you finalize visuals.

anya (A11y): will do. quick a11y checklist: contrast, keyboard focus for all interactive controls, tooltip accessible, heatmap fallback table role=grid, meaningful aria-labels for axis controls.

sam (Eng-Frontend): cross-browser question: heatmap uses canvas for perf — canvas needs offscreen DOM fallback for a11y. we'll implement both and hide one depending on user agent / assistive tech.

jake (Design): small copy tweak proposal for the time-slicer: change "Custom range" to "Choose time range" — clearer to new users.

maria (Product): +1. and add microcopy under sampling dropdown: "Lower sampling reduces cost but may hide rare latency spikes." short and clear.

katie (PM): rollout plan: A) Internally test in canary org; B) Enable for SRE power users; C) Gradual ramp. Note metrics to watch: average time to detect latency regression, clicks to expand card, sampling overrides count.

ui-bot: deploy-preview ready at https://staging.redwood/preview/latency-card/1765432100 — notes: heatmap behind feature flag `heatmap_v2`

li (Eng-ML): one last thought — show an inline note if sampling is too low to surface p99 (e.g., "Insufficient sample to show p99 reliably").

jake (Design): good call. we'll add an inline helper that appears when sample_estimate < 5%. copy: "Low sample rate — p99 may be unreliable."

maria (Product): thanks everyone. next steps: anya + jake produce final assets by EOD Thursday, sam to stub endpoints, li to provide sample_estimate field. will follow up in the thread with updated figma link. :thumbsup:
